title: Add a vignette to an image

seo.metaTitle: Vignette PNG Online - Darken Edges, Free, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Add a vignette to an image in your browser: the edges darken smoothly while the center stays untouched. Free, no upload, no signup.
seo.longDescription: A vignette darkens the outer part of an image and leaves the middle alone, the way a lens shades the corners of a photograph. The falloff is smooth rather than a hard frame, which is why it reads as a photographic effect instead of a border. It is a quick way to focus attention on the middle of a photo, to match a caption to an image, or to hide the edges of a composite. The effect is computed in your browser and the image is never uploaded.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set the strength: zero leaves the image alone, higher values darken the edges more.
Check the preview; the center should stay as bright as the source.
Download the result in the format you need from the Download button.

faq.q: Does the vignette touch the center of the image?
faq.a: No. The darkening grows towards the edges and falls to nothing in the middle, so the subject stays as bright as it was in the original.

faq.q: What does the strength setting do?
faq.a: It sets how dark the corners become. At 0 the image is unchanged; as the value rises the edges deepen. Because the falloff is smooth, there is no edge where the darkening suddenly starts.

faq.q: Why does my picture look banded after a strong vignette?
faq.a: Very dark areas have fewer color steps available, so the smooth gradient can break into visible rings in an 8-bit image. A gentler strength, or saving the result as a high quality JPG or WebP, reduces it.
